hook_text: Six sweets. You eat one. The packet now remembers — and that memory is worth marks.
clip_script: A packet of six sweets: four orange, two mint. You take one, eat it, take another. Simple? Here's what almost everyone misses: the packet REMEMBERS. First draw — four out of six for orange. But the second draw never faces six sweets. It faces five survivors — and WHICH five depends on what you just ate. Ate an orange? Three orange, two mint left. Ate a mint? Four orange, one mint — the odds just moved. That's what 'without replacement' really means: every branch of the story carries brand-new arithmetic. A tree diagram is just the story drawn with its worlds attached. Then two moves finish everything. AND multiplies along a path: orange then orange is four sixths times three fifths — two fifths. OR adds across paths: one of each flavour happens two ways, eight thirtieths plus eight thirtieths — eight fifteenths. And here's the pro move nobody uses: add ALL your path products at the end. They must total exactly one — every possible future accounted for. Thirty thirtieths. If yours don't hit one, the tree just told you which branch is broken. Free receipt, every single question.
visual_style: A crinkly sweet packet spills into an animated branching tree; each branch grows a tiny inventory tag of remaining sweets, path probabilities light up and multiply, and a till-slip receipt prints '30/30 = 1' at the end.
pacing: Quick setup, beat on 'the packet REMEMBERS', rhythmic multiply-along add-across chant, confident receipt reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make trees, tables and triple Venns do the thinking for you.
